definition: A neural network layer that replaces fixed activation functions with learnable Fourier series: φ(x) = a₀ + Σₖ [aₖ·cos(kx) + bₖ·sin(kx)], where each input-output pair has independent learnable coefficients
theoretical_basis: Kolmogorov-Arnold Representation Theorem: any multivariate continuous function can be represented as a superposition of continuous functions of one variable
assumptions: Fourier series can approximate the optimal univariate functions in the KA representation
Learnable frequency scaling adapts to data distribution
invariants: Each input-output pair has independent activation function
Activation functions are parameterized as Fourier series
non_negotiable_steps: Fourier basis computation (cos and sin terms)
Summation over input features following KA theorem structure
key_differences_from_MLP: MLP: fixed activation (ReLU) + learnable linear weights
KAN has stronger theoretical approximation guarantees
deviations: Used GCN (not GAT) for message passing backbone - simpler and more standard
Used 8 Fourier frequencies instead of potentially larger basis
CPU-only training limited epochs and dataset sizes for HIV and MUV
